scenarios.relearn: Clinics don't report you and testing can be free; those fears are myths.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two lines that pressure, not respect.

scene.text: "Let's both test before we go further"
"If you really trusted me you'd skip the test"
"Asking to test means you don't trust me"
"Testing together is just looking after each other"

scenarios.why: Both trick lines weaponise trust to dodge testing; that's pressure, not care.
scenarios.relearn: 'Trust me, skip the test' is pressure; asking to test is mutual care.

scenarios.hook: You and your partner Ritvik are getting closer, and you'd like you both to test first.
scenarios.setup: You bring it up on a quiet evening walk.

steps.prompt: Ritvik says: "Testing? That kind of kills the mood, no?"

options.text: "You're right. Asking makes it sound like I don't trust you."
options.then: Ritvik nods, then frowns. "Wait. Why did you want it, though?"

options.text: "Caring for each other is part of this. Let's both test."
options.then: Ritvik slows down. "Okay. I hadn't thought of it like that."

options.text: "If you won't test, you must be hiding something."
options.then: Ritvik stops walking. "Wow. Is that what you think of me?"

options.text: "Fine. We'll just be careful instead."
options.then: Ritvik nods, and neither of you says what careful means.

steps.why: Testing together is care, not a mood-killer. Saying so keeps the talk warm.

steps.prompt: Ritvik asks: "Does this mean you think I've been with lots of people?"

options.text: "Well, have you?"
options.then: Ritvik's face closes. "I'm not answering that."

options.text: "Maybe. I mean, I don't really know much about your past."
options.then: Ritvik goes quiet, hurt, and the walk turns awkward.

options.text: "No. It's just normal health care for both of us."
options.then: Ritvik relaxes. "Okay. That makes sense."

options.text: "Forget it. Let's not get into all that."
options.then: Ritvik pauses. "No, I want to understand this properly."

steps.why: Testing is about health, not suspicion. Saying so clears the misunderstanding.

steps.prompt: Ritvik admits: "Clinics make me nervous. I'd feel weird walking into one."

options.text: "Then I'll go, and you can skip it."
options.then: Ritvik shrugs. Only half the plan happens.

options.text: "Just use a self-test whenever you feel like it."
options.then: Ritvik nods, but neither of you knows when it would be accurate.

options.text: "Get over it. It's not a big deal."
options.then: Ritvik bristles. "Easy for you to say."

options.text: "Let's ask a counsellor where to go, and go together."
options.then: Ritvik smiles a little. "Together sounds less weird."

steps.why: Going together, with a counsellor's help, makes the clinic feel normal for you both.

steps.prompt: Ritvik asks: "So where does that leave us for now?"

options.text: "Testing can wait. Let's not slow down."
options.then: Ritvik hesitates. "Then why bring it up at all?"

options.text: "Whatever you want is fine with me."
options.then: Ritvik looks unsure. He wanted to hear what you think.

options.text: "We take our time. There's no rush for anything."
options.then: Ritvik laughs. "Okay. No rush." He takes your hand.

options.text: "Let's not talk about it. It's awkward."
options.then: The silence lasts the rest of the walk.

steps.why: Taking your time is always okay, and agreeing on it together is part of care.

scenarios.relearn: Testing together is part of caring for each other, not a mood-killer.

scenarios.hook: You've come to an ICTC centre to get tested, and it's your turn at the desk.
scenarios.setup: The staff member looks up and smiles.

steps.prompt: The staff member asks: "Hello. How can I help you today?"

options.text: "Um, it's for a friend. Never mind."
options.then: She tilts her head. "Lots of people say that. Would you like a test yourself?"

options.text: "Sorry, I think I'm in the wrong place."
options.then: "You might not be," she says gently. "Most people here come for a test."

options.text: "Hi, I'd like to get tested today, please."
options.then: "Of course," she says, and hands you a short form.

options.text: "I'll just take a leaflet for now, thanks."
options.then: She hands one over. "The test is quick, if you'd like to start the form."

steps.why: A plain request is all it takes. Staff here help people test every day.

steps.prompt: She asks: "If you decide to test, can I take your name and age?"

options.text: "Can I give a fake name?"
options.then: She pauses. "Is something about the form worrying you?"

options.text: "Sure. Will this stay confidential?"
options.then: "Yes," she says. "Your details stay confidential here."

options.text: "Actually, I'll come back another time."
options.then: She nods. "Of course. Would you like to meet the counsellor first, at least?"

options.text: "Why do you need that? Who's going to see it?"
options.then: She explains calmly, but you've already tensed up.

steps.why: Giving your details and asking about privacy gets you the facts: ICTC is confidential.

steps.prompt: The counsellor asks: "What questions do you have about the test?"

options.text: "None, really. Let's just get it over with quickly."
options.then: The test goes smoothly, but you leave with questions you didn't ask.

options.text: "Do I really need to? I'm probably fine."
options.then: She smiles. "Lots of people feel that. Testing is how you know."

options.text: "When do I get the result, and what then?"
options.then: She explains both clearly. You feel ready.

options.text: "Can you just tell me it'll be negative?"
options.then: She shakes her head kindly. "I can't promise that, but I'll help either way."

steps.why: Asking about the result and next steps means you know what to expect.

scenarios.relearn: A plain 'I'd like to get tested' is all you need; staff expect it.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Imran calls late at night. He's scared to get tested.
scenarios.setup: His voice is shaky.

steps.prompt: Imran asks: "What do you think? Should I even bother?"

options.text: "Maybe it's better not to know, honestly. Less stress."
options.then: Imran sounds relieved. "Yeah. Maybe." Then he goes quiet again.

options.text: "Try not to think about it too much."
options.then: "Easy to say," he mutters. "It's all I think about."

options.text: "Knowing means you can act, and treatment works."
options.then: Imran is quiet. "I didn't know it was that simple."

options.text: "You'll be fine. You're overthinking it."
options.then: Imran sighs. "You don't know that."

steps.why: Knowing lets him get care, and treatment works. That makes the test worth it.

steps.prompt: Imran says: "I'm scared to go alone. What if someone sees me?"

options.text: "Nobody will notice. Just go."
options.then: Imran goes quiet. He doesn't sound convinced.

options.text: "Wear a mask and cap so no one recognises you."
options.then: Imran laughs nervously. "So it is something to hide."

options.text: "I'll come with you. ICTC centres are confidential."
options.then: Imran breathes out. "You'd really come?"

options.text: "Go somewhere far away, where nobody knows you."
options.then: Imran sighs. "I can't get that far without my parents asking."

steps.why: Company, and knowing the care is confidential, make the first step easier.

steps.prompt: Imran asks: "Should I tell my parents first?"

options.text: "No way. Keep this away from every adult you know."
options.then: Imran agrees, and feels even more alone with it.

options.text: "Yes, and you have to tell them tonight."
options.then: Imran panics. "Tonight? I can't."

options.text: "An adult you trust could really help."
options.then: Imran thinks. "My uncle would get it. Maybe him."

options.text: "I'll tell them for you, if you like."
options.then: Imran goes silent. "No. That's not what I meant."

steps.why: A trusted adult can support him, and he chooses who and when.

scenarios.relearn: Reassure a scared friend: knowing means you can act, and treatment works.

scenarios.hook: In the canteen, word goes round that Harpreet went for an STI test.
scenarios.setup: Your classmate Neel smirks at the table.

steps.prompt: Neel says: "Only dirty people need to get tested."

options.text: "Whatever. Honestly, it's none of my business either way."
options.then: Neel takes your shrug as a green light and keeps going.

options.text: "Yeah, that's a bit weird, I guess."
options.then: Neel grins. "See? Even you think so."

options.text: "Testing is self-care. That's strength, not shame."
options.then: Neel shrugs. "If you say so." A couple of people stop laughing.

options.text: "You'd know all about being dirty, Neel."
options.then: The table laughs, and now it's a fight instead of a point.

steps.why: Calling testing self-care flips the shame back into strength.

steps.prompt: Neel asks the table: "Would any of you actually go and get tested?"

options.text: "Me? No way. I'm not like that, obviously."
options.then: Neel nods. "Exactly. Normal people don't."

options.text: "Sure. It's just a health check, like any other."
options.then: Neel blinks. He hadn't expected a yes.

options.text: "Only if I really had to."
options.then: Neel smirks. "So, if you'd done something."

options.text: "Why, are you asking me to come along with you?"
options.then: The table laughs, and the point gets lost in the joke.

steps.why: Treating testing as ordinary is the clearest answer to shame.

steps.prompt: Later, Harpreet asks you quietly: "Is everyone talking about me?"

options.text: "No, nobody's said a thing about it."
options.then: Harpreet relaxes, then hears the jokes in the corridor an hour later.

options.text: "Yes. Why did you tell anyone you went?"
options.then: Harpreet flinches. "I didn't. Someone saw me."

options.text: "A bit. You've nothing to be ashamed of. Shall we tell a teacher?"
options.then: Harpreet's shoulders drop. "Thanks. Maybe, if it keeps up."

options.text: "Just ignore them. They'll get bored and move on."
options.then: Harpreet nods, but she eats lunch alone the next day.

steps.why: Honesty, solidarity and a trusted adult mean she doesn't face the gossip alone.

scenarios.relearn: Testing is responsible self-care; that's strength, not shame.

scenarios.hook: You and Mira have been seeing each other a few weeks, and you've suggested you both test.
scenarios.setup: Mira looks puzzled.

steps.prompt: Mira asks: "Why test first? Don't you trust me?"

options.text: "No reason. Forget it if it's weird."
options.then: Mira shrugs. "It's not weird. I just don't know much about testing."

options.text: "I don't know. Maybe we don't need to."
options.then: Mira pauses. "Maybe. Honestly, I've never thought about it."

options.text: "I just want to be sure you're clean."
options.then: Mira stiffens. "Clean? Ugly word." She takes a breath. "Still, testing might not be a bad idea."

options.text: "I do. It's just care, for both of us."
options.then: Mira's face softens. "Okay. I guess that's fair."

steps.why: Framing it as care, not suspicion, keeps the talk honest and warm.

steps.prompt: Mira says: "I've never been tested. I wouldn't know where to start."

options.text: "It's easy. Just look it up."
options.then: Mira nods, but the search never happens.

options.text: "Neither have I. Let's find out together."
options.then: Mira laughs. "Okay. A joint project, then."

options.text: "You should have done it by now."
options.then: Mira looks stung. "Well, I haven't."

options.text: "Then let's skip it. It's too complicated."
options.then: Mira hesitates. "Maybe. But one thing still worries me."

steps.why: Starting together makes testing a shared step, not a test of each other.

steps.prompt: Mira asks: "What happens if one of us is positive, though?"

options.text: "Then it's over, I suppose."
options.then: Mira's face falls. "That's harsh."

options.text: "That just won't happen to people like us."
options.then: Mira frowns. "You can't know that."

options.text: "Then we see a doctor. Treatment works."
options.then: Mira nods slowly. "Okay. That's less scary than I thought."

options.text: "Let's not think about that. It's too depressing."
options.then: The question hangs between you for the rest of the evening.

steps.why: A positive result means getting care, and treatment works. It's information, not an ending.

scenarios.relearn: Wanting to both test first is mutual care and an honest start.

scenarios.hook: You're heading out to get tested at the ICTC, and you'd rather keep it private.
scenarios.setup: Your mother looks up from the kitchen as you grab your bag.

steps.prompt: Your mother asks: "Where are you off to so early?"

options.text: "Just a routine health check-up. I'll be back soon."
options.then: She nods. "Okay. Eat something when you're back."

options.text: "To Riya's place. We're studying."
options.then: "Okay," she says. "Say hi to her mother for me."

options.text: "Ugh, can you stop interrogating me?"
options.then: She goes quiet, hurt. "I was only asking, beta."

options.text: "A check-up. Please don't ask me anything else."
options.then: Her eyebrows go up. "Now I'm worried. What kind of check-up?"

steps.why: A calm, true answer keeps your privacy without a lie or a fight.

steps.prompt: That evening she says: "You seemed tense today. Everything okay?"

options.text: "Why does everyone keep asking me things?"
options.then: She sighs. "Because we care. Fine, I'll leave it."

options.text: "I'm fine. You don't need to worry about my health."
options.then: "I'm your mother. I'll always worry a little," she says, unconvinced.

options.text: "I'm okay. If I ever need help, I'll come to you."
options.then: She smiles. "Good. You can, any time."

options.text: "Mostly. Can I explain everything some other day?"
options.then: "Explain what?" she asks, now properly worried.

steps.why: You keep your privacy and still leave the door open to a trusted adult.

steps.prompt: At dinner your cousin Kunal teases: "Mystery trip this morning? Spill."

options.text: "None of your business, Kunal."
options.then: "Ooh, touchy," he grins, and now the whole table is looking.

options.text: "I had a secret date, if you must know."
options.then: Kunal hoots, and the teasing lasts the whole meal.

options.text: "Just a health check-up. Pass the dal?"
options.then: Kunal shrugs. "Boring." The table moves on.

options.text: "Nothing. Can we talk about something else?"
options.then: Kunal raises an eyebrow. "Okay, now I'm curious."

steps.why: A plain, boring answer ends the curiosity. Your health is yours to share or not.

scenarios.relearn: Your status is yours; 'a routine health check-up' keeps it private and calm.

scenarios.hook: You've come to the chemist near your coaching centre to buy an HIV self-test.
scenarios.setup: The shop is busy, and you feel a little shy.

steps.prompt: The pharmacist asks: "Can I help you find something?"

options.text: "No, no. I was just looking around."
options.then: He shrugs and turns to the next customer. The kits stay on the shelf.

options.text: "Some cough syrup, please."
options.then: He hands you a bottle. You leave with syrup and no test.

options.text: "Yes, please. I'm looking for an HIV self-test."
options.then: He nods and reaches behind the counter. "This one. The leaflet's inside."

options.text: "Do you have, um, that test thing? You know."
options.then: He looks puzzled. "Which test? There are many."

steps.why: Naming it plainly gets you what you need in seconds. It's a routine buy.

steps.prompt: Later your friend Dev texts: "Those home kits are useless. Don't waste money."

options.text: "Maybe you're right. I'll skip it."
options.then: Dev sends a thumbs up. The question of your status stays open.

options.text: "They're reliable if you use them right."
options.then: Dev replies: "Wait, really? Where did you read that?"

options.text: "I'll just wait and see if I get any symptoms."
options.then: "Same," Dev replies. Neither of you knows anything more.

options.text: "Then I'll go to a clinic someday instead."
options.then: "Cool," Dev says. Someday has no date on it yet.

steps.why: Self-tests are reliable when used correctly and read after the window period.

steps.prompt: A week later Dev messages: "Okay, say someone does test. When?"

options.text: "Right away. Sooner is always better."
options.then: "Easy," Dev replies. You both assume a test works the same any day.

options.text: "Only if something feels off."

options.text: Call Karthik an idiot, loudly, in front of everyone

options.text: Say: "Knowing my status is the strong move."
options.then: A couple of guys go quiet. One says: "True, actually."

options.text: Roll my eyes and say nothing
options.then: Nobody notices, and the joke stands.

steps.why: Calling testing strength, plainly, reframes it for the whole table.

steps.prompt: Later your friend Senthil quietly asks how testing even works. What do you say?

options.text: "Only people with something to hide get tested."
options.then: Senthil laughs awkwardly and drops it.

options.text: "Karthik's right. It's not for guys like us."
options.then: Senthil nods, and his question goes unasked.

options.text: "Just Google it. That's what I'd do."
options.then: Senthil finds a scary forum and gets more worried.

options.text: "It's routine. I'll show you where to go."
options.then: Senthil leans in. "Okay. Where do you even start?"

steps.why: Sharing calmly can help a friend who's quietly curious take a step.

steps.prompt: A week later Karthik makes the same joke again. What do you do?

options.text: Laugh along, just to avoid a scene
options.then: The joke sticks around another week.

options.text: Message the group later to say Karthik's wrong
options.then: The chat argues for an hour, and the joke still gets made at lunch.

options.text: Say calmly that testing is strength
options.then: Someone else at the table backs you up.

options.text: Leave the table whenever the topic comes up
options.then: Karthik notices and makes it a running joke.

steps.why: Calm, repeated pushback rewrites the room's script over time.

scenarios.hook: You've made it to the ICTC, but your hands are sweating.
scenarios.setup: You reach the counter as the queue moves up.

steps.prompt: The staff member at the counter asks: "Yes? How can I help?"

options.text: "Sorry, never mind. Wrong place."
options.then: She shrugs. At the gate you stop, take a breath and turn back.

options.text: "I'm asking for a friend. She's too shy to come."
options.then: "Then she'll need to come in herself," she says kindly. You nod, and stay.

options.text: "I'd like a routine HIV and STI test, please."
options.then: She nods. "Take a seat. The counsellor will call you."

options.text: "Is there a form, so I don't have to say it?"
options.then: "There is, but just tell me what you need," she says.

steps.why: Saying it plainly is all it takes. Staff hear this request every day.

steps.prompt: The counsellor asks: "Is this your first test?"

options.text: "Yes, and only because I did something stupid."
options.then: She says gently: "Testing isn't a punishment. Let's start."

options.text: "Does it matter? Can we just get it done?"
options.then: "It helps me explain things," she says, a little surprised.

options.text: "Yes. I want a baseline, to know where I stand."
options.then: She nods. "A starting point. Let's talk through what happens."

options.text: "Yes. Can't you just tell me if I'm fine?"
options.then: She shakes her head. "Only a test can tell. That's why we do it."

steps.why: Seeing it as a baseline frames testing as self-care, not shame.

steps.prompt: The counsellor asks: "Any questions before we begin?"

options.text: "No. Let's just get it over with, please."
options.then: "Okay," she says. Your worries stay unspoken.

options.text: "Actually, can I come back another day instead?"
options.then: "You can," she says, "but you're already here."

options.text: "Just one. Roughly how long is the wait?"
options.then: "Twenty minutes," she says. Your bigger worry stays unasked.

options.text: "Yes. Will my result stay confidential?"
options.then: "Yes," she says, and explains exactly how.

steps.why: Asking about privacy settles the worry, so you can test with confidence.

scenarios.relearn: A plain, routine ask gets you tested with no fuss.

scenarios.hook: You and Rehan have been together a few months, and things are getting closer.
scenarios.setup: You're walking home together after class.

steps.prompt: Rehan says: "I really like where this is going."

options.text: "Me too. Let's just see where it goes."
options.then: He smiles and takes your hand. The testing question stays in your head.

options.text: "Me too. But first, have you been with anyone before?"
options.then: He tenses. "Why? Is that a problem?"

options.text: "Me too. Before we go further, shall we both test?"
options.then: He blinks, then nods. "Okay. I hadn't thought of that."

options.text: "Me too. I'll get tested, but you don't need to."
options.then: "Okay," he says. Only half the picture gets checked.

steps.why: A warm 'let's both test' opens the talk as care, not suspicion.

steps.prompt: When you talk about testing a few days later, Rehan asks: "Do you think I have something?"

options.text: "No. It's just care, for both of us."
options.then: He relaxes. "Okay. When you put it like that."

options.text: "I don't know. Maybe? That's why I asked."
options.then: He frowns. "So you do think I might."

options.text: "Of course not. Just forget I even asked."
options.then: He looks relieved, and the plan dissolves.

options.text: "Well, you were with Neel before me, weren't you?"
options.then: His face falls. "Wow. Okay."

steps.why: Testing is mutual care and normal health practice, not an accusation.

steps.prompt: Rehan asks: "Isn't talking about this a bit of a mood-killer?"

options.text: "Yeah, a bit. Let's just get it over with."
options.then: He nods. The talk starts to feel like a chore.

options.text: "Only if you make it weird."
options.then: "I'm not making it weird," he says, a bit stung.

options.text: "Maybe. Let's only talk about it if it ever comes up."
options.then: "Sure," he says, and the talk drifts to films.

options.text: "Not to me. Caring for each other is part of it."
options.then: He grins. "Okay. That's actually kind of sweet."

steps.why: Talking about testing is care, and a caring partner welcomes it.

steps.prompt: The next weekend Rehan asks: "So where would we even go?"

options.text: "A private lab. Your parents can pay."
options.then: He laughs nervously. "My parents would ask why."

options.text: "An ICTC. It's free and confidential."
options.then: "Free? Saturday, then," he says. "Coffee after?"

options.text: "I'll figure it out and let you know."
options.then: "Okay," he says. A week passes without a plan.

options.text: "Nowhere. Honestly, let's skip it."
options.then: He shrugs. "Okay, if you're sure."

steps.why: Knowing where to go turns a good talk into a real plan.

steps.prompt: Later Rehan asks quietly: "If we test, what if one of us is positive?"

options.text: "Then it's over between us, I guess."
options.then: He looks stung. "Just like that?"

options.text: "Don't even say that. We'll be fine."
options.then: He nods, but the worry stays on his face.

options.text: "Then we'd get treatment and work it out together."
options.then: He squeezes your hand. "Okay. That makes it less scary."

options.text: "We'd sort it out somehow. Let's not talk about it now."
options.then: "Sure," he says, though he clearly wanted to talk.

steps.why: Most STIs are treatable and HIV is manageable. Facing it together is care.

scenarios.relearn: A warm 'let's both test' opens the conversation as care.

scenarios.hook: You and your partner Tanya are getting close, and you've brought up using protection.
scenarios.setup: You're sitting together in the park after class.

steps.prompt: Tanya laughs and says: "We don't need it, do we? We trust each other."

options.text: "I guess trust is what really matters."
options.then: She smiles, relieved. Protection stays unspoken.

options.text: "I trust you, and I'd still like protection."
options.then: She pauses. "Okay. I didn't know it mattered that much."

options.text: "Maybe asking makes it look like I don't trust you."
options.then: "Exactly," she says. The topic slides away.

options.text: "Let's talk about it some other time."
options.then: "Sure," she says, and the topic slides for now.

steps.why: Trust and protection go together. Saying it kindly keeps both.

steps.prompt: A few days later Tanya asks: "Doesn't protection ruin the moment, though?"

options.text: "Maybe you're right. I'm overthinking it."
options.then: She nods, then looks at you. "You don't sound sure."

options.text: "Not for me. Feeling safe makes it better."
options.then: She thinks. "Okay. That's fair."

options.text: "Ruin it? So you don't care how I feel?"
options.then: She pulls back. "That's not fair."

options.text: "My friends say I have to, so that's why I'm asking."
options.then: "Your friends?" she asks. "So it's their rule?"

steps.why: Protection is care. It doesn't ruin intimacy, and you can say so.

steps.prompt: Later Tanya asks: "Honestly, what if we just see this differently?"

options.text: "Then maybe protection isn't that important."
options.then: She smiles. Your line feels softer than you meant it to.

options.text: "Then maybe I'm asking for too much."
options.then: She shrugs. "Maybe." The question quietly stops being yours.

options.text: "Let's not think about that yet."
options.then: "Fine," she says. The question waits for a harder moment.

options.text: "Then we wait. That's fine with me."
options.then: She nods slowly. "Okay. I'd rather we agree, then."

steps.why: Holding your line kindly, with waiting as a real option, is care and consent.

scenarios.relearn: Hold the protection line kindly but firmly.

scenarios.hook: Your partner Manav says he has something important to tell you, and his hands are shaking.
scenarios.setup: You're sitting on the steps outside his building.

steps.prompt: Manav says: "I tested last week. I have an STI. I've started treatment."

options.text: "How could you not tell me sooner?"
options.then: He flinches. "I only found out last week."

options.text: "I can't deal with this right now."
options.then: He nods, eyes down. "Okay. I understand."

options.text: "Thank you for telling me. Let's work it out."
options.then: He exhales. "I was so scared you'd walk away."

options.text: "It's fine, really. Let's not make it a big deal."
options.then: He looks unsure. "But we kind of need to talk about it."

steps.why: Thanking him for his honesty meets a disclosure with dignity.

steps.prompt: Manav asks: "Do you think I'm disgusting now?"

options.text: "No. It's a health thing, not who you are."
options.then: His shoulders drop. "Thank you. I needed to hear that."

options.text: "No. But I need to know who you got it from."
options.then: He stiffens. "Does that change anything?"

options.text: "Of course not. Let's never mention it again."
options.then: He nods, but the worry stays in his eyes.

options.text: "No. But I'll need time before I trust you again."
options.then: His face falls. "Trust? I told you as soon as I knew."

steps.why: An STI says nothing about a person's worth. Saying so lifts the shame.

steps.prompt: Manav asks: "Should you get tested too?"

options.text: "No. I feel fine, so I must be fine."
options.then: He looks worried. "Mine had no signs at all."

options.text: "Yes. I'll book one, and follow the doctor's advice."
options.then: He nods. "I'll come with you if you want."

options.text: "Only if you pay for it, since it's your fault anyway."
options.then: He goes quiet. "Okay. If that's how you see it."

options.text: "Maybe later. Let's wait and see."
options.then: "Okay," he says, unsure. The test stays unbooked.

steps.why: Testing and following a doctor's advice is the safe way, for both of you.

steps.prompt: A week later Manav asks: "Have you told anyone about me?"

options.text: "Only my best friend. She won't tell anyone."
options.then: His face drops. "You told someone?"

options.text: "No. It's yours to share, not mine."
options.then: He smiles, relieved. "Thank you. That means a lot."

options.text: "Not yet. My family will ask, though."
options.then: He looks scared. "Please don't tell them."

options.text: "No. But you tell your ex, or I will."
options.then: He goes pale. "I'll handle it. Please don't."

steps.why: Someone's status is private. Keeping it so is respect and dignity.

scenarios.relearn: Meet a disclosure with dignity and a plan, not panic.

scenarios.hook: Ishita, your 14-year-old neighbour, hints that an older boy is pressuring her for secret 'favours'.
scenarios.setup: She looks scared and won't meet your eyes.

steps.prompt: Ishita asks: "Promise you won't tell anyone?"

options.text: "I promise. It stays between us."
options.then: She relaxes a little. Now only you know.

options.text: "Why didn't you just say no to him in the first place?"
options.then: Her eyes fill. "I knew you'd think it was me."

options.text: "Tell me everything first, then I'll decide."
options.then: She shrinks back. "I don't want to say it all."

options.text: "I can't promise that. But this isn't your fault."
options.then: She hesitates. "Okay. But I'm really scared."

steps.why: Never promise to keep an unsafe secret. Saying it's not her fault keeps her talking.

steps.prompt: Ishita whispers: "He says I owe him because he bought me things."

options.text: "Maybe just keep him happy for now."
options.then: She nods slowly, looking more trapped.

options.text: "You don't owe him anything. It's not on you."
options.then: She looks up. "Really? He made it sound like I did."

options.text: "Give the things back and he'll leave you alone."
options.then: She shakes her head. "He'll just get angry."

options.text: "I'll go and talk to him myself and sort it."
options.then: Her eyes widen. "No! Then he'll know I told."

steps.why: Gifts never buy a person. Telling her it isn't her fault matters most.

steps.prompt: Ishita asks: "So what do we even do?"

options.text: "Let's handle it ourselves and keep the adults out of it."
options.then: She nods. Now two of you carry it, and no adult knows.

options.text: "Let's post about him so everyone knows."
options.then: Her face goes white. "He'll find out it was me."

options.text: "Let's tell a trusted adult together, like your mum."
options.then: She takes a breath. "Will you sit with me when I tell her?"

options.text: "Let's wait and see if he stops on his own."
options.then: A week later he's waiting outside her tuition again.

steps.why: A trusted adult can protect her. Going together means she isn't alone.

steps.prompt: Ishita asks: "What if I tell an adult and they don't believe me?"

options.text: "Then we'll just forget it."
options.then: She looks crushed. "So it's hopeless?"

options.text: "They will. Don't worry about it."
options.then: "How do you know?" Ishita whispers.

options.text: "Then you'll have to sort it yourself."
options.then: Ishita goes quiet, her hands shaking.

options.text: "Then we call Childline 1098 together."
options.then: She nods, a little steadier. "Okay. Together."

steps.why: There's always another safe adult or Childline 1098. She never carries this alone.

scenarios.relearn: Name it as not-their-fault and point to a trusted adult or Childline.

scenarios.hook: You've read about PrEP and want to ask a doctor if it's right for you.
scenarios.setup: You sit down across from Dr Rao, and your mind goes blank.

steps.prompt: Dr Rao asks: "So, what brings you in today?"

options.text: "Just a cold, I think."
options.then: She checks your throat, then asks if there's anything else. You mention PrEP.

options.text: "My friend wants to know about PrEP."
options.then: "Or is it for you?" she asks kindly. You nod.

options.text: "I'd like to ask whether PrEP is right for me."
options.then: She pulls her chair closer. "Let's go through it."

options.text: "I want PrEP. Can you just write it up for me?"
options.then: She smiles. "First, let's see whether it fits you."

steps.why: Asking directly is routine for a doctor and gets you real answers.

steps.prompt: Dr Rao asks: "What do you already know about it?"

options.text: "That it protects you against basically everything."
options.then: She shakes her head. "Only HIV. Not other STIs or pregnancy."

options.text: "That it prevents HIV, but not how it fits me."
options.then: She nods. "Let me explain what it covers and what it doesn't."

options.text: "Nothing really. I'll just take your word for it."
options.then: She pauses. "I'd like you to understand it too."

options.text: "A forum said it's just one pill and you're all set."
options.then: "Not quite," she says. "It needs regular check-ins."

steps.why: Sharing what you know lets the doctor fill the gaps and correct myths.

steps.prompt: Dr Rao says: "It means regular visits and tests. How does that sound?"

options.text: "Too much effort. Forget it."
options.then: "It's your choice," she says. "The door's open if you change your mind."

options.text: "Doable. The check-ins can be part of my stack."
options.then: She nods. "Then let's plan your first visit. Bring someone you trust, if you like."

options.text: "Can I skip the tests and just take it?"
options.then: "No. The tests are part of keeping you safe on it," she says.

options.text: "Fine. Then I'll use it instead of condoms from now on."
options.then: She pauses. "Condoms still matter for other STIs."

steps.why: PrEP's routine is part of owning your prevention.

scenarios.relearn: Ask the doctor directly; it's a routine question for them.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Selvam has decided STI testing is a waste of time.
scenarios.setup: You're walking home from tuition together.

steps.prompt: Selvam says: "Seriously. You'd see it on someone, right?"

options.text: "Not really. Many infections show no signs."
options.then: Selvam frowns. "No signs at all? I didn't know that."

options.text: "Yeah, mostly. You'd notice something off."
options.then: "See?" he grins. "Testing is for people who look sick."

options.text: "Maybe. I'm not a doctor, so who knows?"
options.then: He shrugs. "Exactly. So why bother?"

options.text: "Only if you look closely enough at them."
options.then: "So I just need to look closely," he laughs.

steps.why: Many STIs have no visible signs, so looking tells you nothing.

steps.prompt: Selvam asks: "Okay, but if someone wanted to know for sure, how would they?"

options.text: "You wait until something feels wrong."
options.then: "Okay," he says. "So I just wait."

options.text: "Only a test tells you. It's quick and routine."
options.then: "Huh. That's it? Just a test?" he asks.

options.text: "Ask your partner if they've had anything."
options.then: "And just believe them?" he asks, doubtful.

options.text: "Look up the symptoms and check yourself."
options.then: "That sounds easier than a clinic," he says.

steps.why: A test is the only way anyone knows their status.

steps.prompt: Selvam asks: "Say I wanted a test. Where would I go without anyone seeing me?"

options.text: "An ICTC, with an adult you trust. It's free."
options.then: Selvam thinks. "Maybe my uncle. Will you show me where it is?"

options.text: "A private lab far away, where no one knows you."
options.then: "That costs money I don't have," he sighs.

options.text: "Wait until you move out for college."
options.then: "That's a year away," he says. "Fine by me."

options.text: "Skip it if you're that worried about it."
options.then: "Yeah," he says, relieved. "Maybe later."

steps.why: ICTC testing is free and private, and a trusted adult makes it easier to go.

steps.prompt: A week later, Selvam asks: "What if people see me there and think I'm sick?"

options.text: "It's a health check. It says nothing about you."
options.then: "Huh," he says. "Like getting your eyes checked."

options.text: "Wear a cap and keep your head down."
options.then: "So I should be embarrassed?" he asks.

options.text: "They might think you did something, honestly."
options.then: Selvam's face drops. "Then forget it."

options.text: "Just tell them you're there for a friend."
options.then: "So I lie?" he says, frowning.

steps.why: Testing is routine self-care, not proof of anything. That takes the shame out.

scenarios.relearn: Correct the myth kindly: only a test tells your status.

scenarios.hook: Your girlfriend Simran says you don't need condoms anymore, since she trusts you.

options.text: "Lots of serious couples use them. Look it up."
options.then: She shrugs. "Okay, but I asked about us."

options.text: "Don't make it weird. It's just a condom."
options.then: Simran looks hurt. "I wasn't making it weird."

scenarios.setup: You're sharing a plate of misal after class.

steps.prompt: Omkar asks: "HPV vaccine? Why do you need that?"

options.text: "It helps prevent some cancers. That's all."
options.then: "Cancers? Oh. I didn't know that," he says.

options.text: "I dunno. A friend mentioned it."
options.then: "So you don't know why you're getting it?" he asks.

options.text: "Don't worry. It's not because of you."
options.then: Omkar blinks. "I wasn't worried until you said that."

options.text: "It's a girls' thing. You wouldn't get it."
options.then: "Try me," he says, a little stung.

steps.why: A plain answer about what it prevents keeps it a normal health choice.

steps.prompt: Omkar asks: "Does that mean you think one of us has something?"

options.text: "No. It's prevention, like any other vaccine."
options.then: He nods. "Like the ones we had as kids?"

options.text: "Not you. I just can't be sure about anyone."
options.then: Omkar frowns. "That sounds a lot like me."

options.text: "Maybe. You can never really know."
options.then: He looks uneasy. "That's a scary way to put it."

options.text: "Don't make this about you, Omkar."
options.then: "I'm just asking," he says, stung.

steps.why: Vaccines are prevention, not a sign that something's wrong.

steps.prompt: Omkar asks: "Should I get it too, then?"

options.text: "Ask a doctor whether it fits you."
options.then: "Okay," he says. "I'll ask at my next check-up."

options.text: "No. It's only for girls."
options.then: He shrugs. "Okay, I'll skip it then."

options.text: "Yes. Everyone has to have it."
options.then: "Has to?" he asks. "Says who?"

options.text: "Only if you've been with someone before."
options.then: Omkar goes red. "Wait, what are you asking?"

steps.why: A doctor can tell him if it fits. That's the same step you took.

scenarios.relearn: The HPV vaccine is a plain health choice you can explain calmly.

scenarios.hook: You've suggested you and Ishaan both get tested before things go further.
scenarios.setup: He's walking you to the bus stop.

steps.prompt: Ishaan says: "Testing? But I feel totally fine."

options.text: "Many infections show no signs. Fine isn't the same as knowing."
options.then: Ishaan pauses. "Seriously? No signs at all?"

options.text: "Okay. If you feel fine, that's good enough."
options.then: Ishaan smiles. "See? Simple." The question stays open.

options.text: "Fine for now. You can't know what you might be carrying."
options.then: Ishaan looks rattled. "Carrying? What's that supposed to mean?"

options.text: "Me too. Let's test only if one of us feels off."
options.then: Ishaan nods. "Deal." Then he frowns, still turning it over.

steps.why: Many STIs are silent, so a test is the only way to actually know.

steps.prompt: Ishaan says: "Also, I've only been with one person before you."

options.text: "One is enough to pass something on, you know."
options.then: Ishaan's ears go red. "Great. Now I feel like I did something wrong."

options.text: "That's okay. Testing's routine, not about numbers."
options.then: Ishaan nods slowly. "Okay. That makes it feel less weird."

options.text: "Then you're probably fine. Forget I asked."
options.then: Ishaan nods, and the plan to test quietly falls away.

options.text: "Who was it? Did she ever get tested?"
options.then: Ishaan stiffens. "That's her business, not ours."

steps.why: Testing is about health, not how many partners anyone has had.

steps.prompt: Days later, Ishaan asks: "If we did test, wouldn't the clinic be awkward?"

options.text: "Probably. Let's go somewhere nobody knows us."
options.then: You plan a long trip across town, and it starts to feel like a secret.

options.text: "It's private. We can ask an adult we trust along."

options.text: "You go first and tell me what it's like."

options.text: "Don't be silly. Nobody cares about that."

steps.why: Testing is private by design, and a trusted adult alongside makes it feel ordinary.

scenarios.hook: "If you're HIV positive you have to give up on having a family."

myth.un: HIV positive means giving up on a family.
myth.re: With treatment, people with HIV plan pregnancies and have HIV-negative babies safely.
myth.why: Treatment keeps the virus undetectable, so it isn't passed on.

scenarios.relearn: With treatment, people with HIV can safely plan a family.

scenarios.hook: "Starting HIV treatment means swallowing a fistful of pills forever."

myth.un: HIV treatment means a fistful of pills forever.
myth.re: Most people take a single daily tablet; some use long-acting injections.
myth.why: Modern regimens are simple, and people stick with them easily.

scenarios.relearn: Modern HIV treatment is often one daily pill, not a handful.

scenarios.hook: "Once you have an STI, you'll always carry it."

myth.un: Once you get an STI you carry it for life.
myth.re: Chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis and trichomoniasis are fully cured with the right medicine.
myth.why: The right antibiotics clear these infections completely.

scenarios.relearn: Four common STIs are fully curable with the right medicine.

scenarios.hook: "HIV treatment is too costly for an ordinary family."

myth.un: HIV treatment costs too much for an ordinary family.
myth.re: In India, HIV treatment is provided free at government ART centres.
myth.why: The national programme makes lifelong treatment reachable for everyone.

scenarios.relearn: HIV treatment is free at government ART centres in India.

scenarios.hook: "If you start HIV medicine, you can never stop or skip a day or you'll die."

myth.un: Skip one day of HIV medicine and you'll die.
myth.re: Taking it regularly keeps you well; a missed dose isn't a disaster, just get back on track.
myth.why: Steady treatment, not panic over one dose, is what keeps the virus down.

scenarios.relearn: Take HIV medicine regularly; one missed dose is recoverable.

scenarios.hook: "There's no medicine for HIV, only for the infections it brings."

myth.un: There's no medicine for HIV itself.
myth.re: Antiretroviral therapy treats HIV directly, keeping the immune system strong.
myth.why: ART acts on the virus, so the infections it used to cause rarely happen.

scenarios.relearn: Antiretroviral therapy treats HIV itself and keeps you well.

scenarios.hook: "An undetectable result just means the test missed it."

myth.un: Undetectable just means the test missed the virus.
myth.re: Undetectable means treatment has pushed the virus too low to measure or pass on.
myth.why: It's a real, measured result that proves the treatment is working.

scenarios.relearn: Undetectable is a real result: too low to measure or transmit.

scenarios.hook: "Treating an STI early or late makes no difference."

myth.un: Treating an STI early or late makes no difference.
myth.re: Early treatment clears it before complications; waiting can affect fertility or health.
myth.why: Acting sooner keeps a simple infection from causing harder problems.

scenarios.relearn: Treat an STI early to avoid complications; timing matters.

scenarios.hook: "A positive result means your life is basically over."

myth.un: A positive result means your life is over.
myth.re: A result is information to act on; with treatment you keep studying, working and loving.
myth.why: Treatment turns a result into a managed part of a full life.

scenarios.relearn: A positive result is information to act on, not the end.

scenarios.hook: "You can feel when HIV treatment is working, so tests are pointless."

myth.un: You can just feel when treatment is working.
myth.re: Regular viral-load tests confirm it's working; feelings alone don't tell you.
myth.why: The number, not a hunch, shows the virus is controlled.

scenarios.relearn: Viral-load tests, not feelings, confirm treatment is working.

scenarios.hook: "Only big-city hospitals can treat HIV."

myth.un: Only big-city hospitals can treat HIV.
myth.re: ART centres and link centres run across districts, so care is reachable near home.
myth.why: The programme is spread out so people don't have to travel far for treatment.

scenarios.relearn: ART care runs across districts, reachable close to home.

scenarios.hook: "Herbal or 'detox' cures clear HIV if you believe in them."

myth.un: Herbal or detox cures can clear HIV.
myth.re: Only proven antiretroviral medicine controls HIV; unproven cures waste time and risk health.
myth.why: Time lost on fake cures is time the virus keeps spreading inside the body.

scenarios.relearn: Only proven ART controls HIV; 'detox cures' don't work.

scenarios.hook: "If a partner is on treatment and undetectable, you still can't be intimate safely."

myth.un: You can't be intimate safely with an undetectable partner.
myth.re: U=U: an undetectable partner cannot pass HIV on sexually.
myth.why: Effective treatment keeps the virus too low to be transmitted.

scenarios.relearn: U=U: an undetectable partner can't pass HIV on sexually.

scenarios.hook: "A treated STI always comes back on its own."

myth.un: A treated STI always returns on its own.
myth.re: A cured STI is gone; you only get it again from a new exposure, not by itself.
myth.why: Cure means the infection is cleared, not lying dormant.

scenarios.relearn: A cured STI is gone; reinfection comes from new exposure only.

scenarios.hook: "People with HIV always look sick, so you'd know to avoid treatment failure."

myth.un: People with HIV always look sick.
myth.re: On treatment, people look and feel well; you can't tell health from appearance.
myth.why: Effective treatment keeps people healthy, with no visible signs.

scenarios.relearn: On treatment, people with HIV look and feel well.

scenarios.hook: "Going to an ART centre means everyone will know your status."

myth.un: Going for treatment means everyone will know.
myth.re: ART care is confidential; your status is private health information.
myth.why: Confidentiality is built into the service so people can get care without fear.

scenarios.relearn: ART care is confidential; your status stays private.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: if a result were positive, what's the first kind thing you'd tell yourself?

scenarios.hook: Lensy: which fact about STIs surprised you most?

scenarios.hook: Lensy: 'undetectable' is a result worth being proud of. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Reaching undetectable is the treatment doing its job, fully worth pride.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what would help most in choosing to act fast on a result, info or support?
scenarios.affirm: Whatever you'd reach for, knowing what helps you act is real self-knowledge.
