scenarios.hook: Your result shows a curable STI, and the doctor writes you a prescription.

steps.prompt: Outside, a friend says a chemist sells a cheaper tablet. What do you do?

options.text: Buy the cheaper tablet your friend means
options.then: The chemist hands it over, but it isn't the one that treats this.

options.text: Get the exact medicine the doctor prescribed
options.then: You collect it and set a daily reminder on your phone.

options.text: Wait and see if it clears up on its own
options.then: Days pass. Nothing feels different, and nothing gets treated.

options.text: Plan to take half the course to save money
options.then: The strip lasts longer, but the infection isn't fully treated.

steps.why: Only the right course cures it. A swap or a guess can leave it untreated.

steps.prompt: That week, your partner Imran asks why you've seemed distant. What do you do?

options.text: Say you're just stressed about exams
options.then: Imran nods, and he has no reason to get tested.

options.text: Accuse him of giving it to you
options.then: Imran is stunned. "I didn't even know. Are you sure?"

options.text: Tell him the result so he can test too
options.then: Imran is quiet, then asks where you got tested.

options.text: Break up by text without saying why
options.then: Imran is hurt and confused, and still untested.

steps.why: Telling him lets him test and treat it too, so it doesn't pass back to you.

steps.prompt: A few days later, your mausi asks why you've seemed so worried. What do you do?

options.text: Say it's just exams, so she won't think less of you
options.then: Mausi nods, unconvinced, and you carry it alone a while longer.

options.text: Tell her about the result and ask for her help
options.then: Mausi squeezes your hand. "It's curable. I'll help with whatever comes next."

options.text: Ask her for a home remedy to speed it up
options.then: Mausi suggests a kadha, and the real treatment slips further down the list.

options.text: Ask her to tell Imran's family for you
options.then: Mausi frowns. "That's private. Should they really hear it from me?"

steps.why: A trusted adult can help you finish treatment and handle what comes next.

scenarios.debrief: Treat it properly, tell recent partners so they can act too, and let a trusted adult help.
scenarios.relearn: On a curable STI: take the prescribed course and tell partners.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Murugan tested HIV positive and says his life is finished.

steps.prompt: He won't look at you as he says it. What do you do?

options.text: Go quiet, unsure what to say
options.then: The silence stretches, and Murugan takes it as agreement.

options.text: Tell him to hide it from everyone forever
options.then: Murugan nods numbly, and the secret starts to feel like a sentence.

options.text: Say treatment works and you're not going anywhere
options.then: Murugan finally looks up. "You mean that?"

options.text: Say lots of people have it, so it's no big deal
options.then: Murugan snaps. "It's a big deal to me."

steps.why: A few true, kind words replace 'finished' with something to hold on to.

steps.prompt: Murugan admits he hasn't gone back to the centre since. What do you do?

options.text: Tell him off for wasting time
options.then: Murugan shuts down. "I knew you'd lecture me."

options.text: Suggest a herbal healer your neighbour trusts
options.then: The healer promises a cure, and the centre visit slides again.

options.text: Say there's no rush, maybe next year
options.then: Murugan nods, relieved, and care gets pushed further back.

options.text: Offer to go with him, and an adult he chooses
options.then: Murugan hesitates, then nods. "My periappa, maybe. Wednesday."

steps.why: Going with him and an adult he picks makes the step easier, and early care works best.

steps.prompt: When Murugan finally goes, he stops at the centre gate. What do you do?

options.text: Sit with him, then walk in together
options.then: After a few minutes, Murugan stands. "Okay. Let's go."

options.text: Tell him to stop being scared and go in
options.then: Murugan's jaw clenches, and he stays outside longer.

options.text: Go in and explain everything for him
options.then: Murugan hears you tell a stranger his news and looks away.

options.text: Suggest coming back another day
options.then: Murugan agrees quickly, and you both head home.

steps.why: Waiting with him lets him walk in on his own terms, with support.

steps.prompt: A month later, Murugan is on treatment but fears his plans for college are gone. What do you do?

options.text: Agree that some plans might be off now
options.then: Murugan sighs, and his plans shrink a little more.

options.text: Tell him not to think so far ahead
options.then: Murugan nods, but the worry stays.

options.text: Remind him people on treatment live full lives
options.then: Murugan pulls out a college brochure. "Still want this one."

options.text: Say he should keep it hidden at college forever
options.then: Murugan nods, and college starts to feel like a place to hide.

steps.why: Treatment lets people live full lives, so his plans are still his.

scenarios.debrief: Treatment works, and showing up replaces 'finished' with hope.
scenarios.relearn: For a newly-diagnosed friend: say treatment works and show up.

scenarios.hook: You've been on HIV treatment for a year, and you feel completely well.

steps.prompt: A friend says feeling this good means you can stop now. What do you do?

options.text: Stop, since you clearly feel fine
options.then: At your next check-up, the doctor looks concerned and asks what changed.

options.text: Take it only on the days you remember
options.then: Some days you forget, and soon you stop keeping track.

options.text: Keep taking it daily, like you have been
options.then: Your routine stays the same, and so does your energy.

options.text: Ask your friend which days you could skip
options.then: Your friend guesses a schedule that no doctor gave you.

steps.why: Feeling well is the treatment working. Taking it daily keeps it that way.

steps.prompt: Your exams clash with your follow-up appointment. What do you do?

options.text: Skip it this time, since you feel fine
options.then: One missed visit turns into two, and no one checks how it's going.

options.text: Call the centre and move it to a nearby date
options.then: The centre finds a slot two days after your last paper.

options.text: Wait for the centre to call and remind you
options.then: No call comes, and the weeks slip by.

options.text: Plan to go in a few months instead
options.then: Months pass, and the visit keeps sliding down your list.

steps.why: Follow-ups check the treatment is still working, so moving one beats missing it.

steps.prompt: On a school trip, you realise you forgot your tablets. What do you do?

options.text: Skip them for the trip and restart at home
options.then: Days pass without them, and you feel uneasy the whole time.

options.text: Ask a friend to explain it to a teacher for you
options.then: Your friend fumbles it, and now two people know more than you meant.

options.text: Buy something similar at a local chemist
options.then: The chemist isn't sure what you need, and you're left guessing at doses.

options.text: Tell a teacher you trust, and call home or the centre
options.then: Your teacher helps you call home, and a dose plan is sorted by evening.

steps.why: A trusted adult can help you get your doses fast, so the gap stays short.

scenarios.debrief: Feeling well means the treatment is working, which is why you keep taking it.
scenarios.relearn: Keep taking HIV treatment when you feel well; that's it working.

scenarios.hook: Your aunt brings a herbal cure for your HIV and says to stop the centre's tablets.

steps.prompt: She means well, and she's waiting for an answer. What do you do?

options.text: Promise to think about switching, to keep the peace
options.then: Your aunt beams, sure you'll come round soon.

options.text: Take both, and keep it from your doctor
options.then: You start both, and a quiet worry about mixing them grows.

options.text: Snap that herbal stuff is total nonsense
options.then: Your aunt's face falls. "I was only trying to help."

options.text: Thank her, and say you're staying on your treatment
options.then: Your aunt purses her lips. "Think about it, at least."

steps.why: A kind 'no thanks' respects her care and protects your health.

steps.prompt: Your aunt says the cure worked for a neighbour. What do you do?

options.text: Agree to try it for one month as a test
options.then: Your aunt is delighted, and a month off treatment starts to feel real.

options.text: Say you'll ask your counsellor at the next visit
options.then: Your aunt shrugs. "Ask, then. But I know what I saw."

options.text: Ask the neighbour for the recipe to be polite
options.then: The neighbour sends a long list, and the pressure grows.

options.text: Tell her the neighbour is lying
options.then: Your aunt bristles. "Why would she lie to me?"

steps.why: Your counsellor can answer doubts with facts, so you stay on care that works.

steps.prompt: At the centre, the counsellor asks if anything is worrying you. What do you do?

options.text: Say all is fine, so your aunt isn't in trouble
options.then: The counsellor nods, and your questions go home unanswered.

options.text: Ask only about side effects, not the cure
options.then: She answers, but the bigger worry stays unspoken.

options.text: Tell her about the cure and ask your doubts
options.then: She explains why it can't replace treatment, and how to tell your aunt.

options.text: Say you might switch, and watch her reaction
options.then: The counsellor looks worried and asks why. You change the subject.

steps.why: Honest questions get honest answers, and she can help you handle your aunt.

steps.prompt: At the next family function, your aunt raises it in front of everyone. What do you do?

options.text: Announce that your doctor says she's wrong
options.then: The room goes quiet, and now everyone is asking questions.

options.text: Quietly say you'll talk to her later, in private
options.then: Your aunt hesitates, then nods and changes the subject.

options.text: Explain your whole diagnosis so they understand
options.then: Relatives nod along, and by evening your status is family news.

options.text: Tell everyone to mind their own business
options.then: A few relatives exchange looks, and the gossip starts anyway.

steps.why: Moving it somewhere private protects your privacy and keeps the talk kind.

scenarios.debrief: Proven treatment works, and a kind 'no thanks' protects you.
scenarios.relearn: Stick with proven HIV treatment; 'cures' risk health.

scenarios.hook: Your HIV self-test shows a reactive result, and the kit says to get it confirmed.

steps.prompt: The thought of walking into a centre makes your stomach drop. What do you do?

options.text: Put it off for a few months until you're calmer
options.then: The weeks drag, and the worry follows you to every class.

options.text: Search forums to work out what it means
options.then: One forum says it's nothing. Another says the worst.

options.text: Plan to go to an ICTC centre or doctor this week
options.then: You look up the nearest centre and note its hours.

options.text: Do a second self-test, then a third, to be sure
options.then: The results confuse you more, and you still haven't seen anyone.

steps.why: A reactive self-test needs a proper test to confirm it, and going soon ends the guessing.

steps.prompt: You don't want to go alone, but you're scared to tell anyone. What do you do?

options.text: Tell your whole friend group so they can help
options.then: Your friends mean well, but now everyone is guessing.

options.text: Tell one adult you trust and ask them to come
options.then: Your aunt listens, squeezes your hand, and clears her Thursday.

options.text: Wait until you can go without anyone knowing
options.then: Waiting for the perfect moment pushes the visit further away.

options.text: Go alone, and tell no one whatever happens
options.then: You sit in the waiting room alone, your heart pounding.

steps.why: A trusted adult can help you get there and hear the answers with you.

steps.prompt: When you get to the centre, the counsellor asks if you have questions. What do you do?

options.text: Nod along and leave as fast as you can
options.then: On the bus home, the questions crowd back in.

options.text: Ask only whether you'll be okay
options.then: She reassures you, but the next steps stay fuzzy.

options.text: Ask her not to tell you anything bad
options.then: She explains gently that knowing helps, but you've stopped listening.

options.text: Ask what the result means and what comes next
options.then: She walks you through the confirmatory test and when you'll know.

steps.why: Clear answers turn worry into a plan you can actually follow.

scenarios.debrief: Free, confidential care turns worry into a clear next step.
scenarios.relearn: Go for free, confidential care soon; it turns worry into a plan.

scenarios.hook: Your partner Shreya is undetectable, but she worries she could still pass HIV to you.

steps.prompt: She says maybe you'd be safer with someone else. What do you do?

options.text: Pull back a bit, just to be safe
options.then: Shreya notices at once, and her worry turns to hurt.

options.text: Say undetectable means it can't pass on through sex
options.then: Shreya looks at you. "You looked it up?" She almost smiles.

options.text: Suggest she gets tested every week to be sure
options.then: Shreya's face falls. "So you don't believe my results."

options.text: Say you'd rather not talk about HIV at all
options.then: Shreya nods, and her fear stays with her, unspoken.

steps.why: U=U is settled science, so her fear doesn't have to come between you.

steps.prompt: Shreya asks if you'd come to her next check-up with her. What do you do?

options.text: Say it's her health, so it's not your place
options.then: Shreya nods slowly, and goes alone again.

options.text: Say yes, but only so you can see her results
options.then: Shreya stiffens. "I'd have told you. You could just ask."

options.text: Say yes, and bring your own questions to ask
options.then: Shreya grins. "Bring a list. Dr Rao loves questions."

options.text: Say you're too busy with exams this month
options.then: Shreya says it's fine, but she sounds let down.

steps.why: Going with her shows trust, and the doctor can answer your questions too.

steps.prompt: Later, a friend warns you that dating someone with HIV is reckless. What do you do?

options.text: Agree to think about whether it's worth it
options.then: The doubt your friend planted follows you to your next date.

options.text: Laugh it off and change the subject
options.then: Your friend takes the laugh as agreement.

options.text: Stop talking to that friend without explaining
options.then: Your friend is baffled, and the myth stays where it was.

options.text: Tell them about U=U, and that it's not for gossip
options.then: Your friend blinks. "Huh. I really didn't know that."

steps.why: Settled science answers the myth, and keeping it out of gossip protects her.

scenarios.debrief: U=U is settled science, so meet it with trust.
scenarios.relearn: With an undetectable partner, U=U means closeness is safe.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two lines that spread fear about treatment (so you can reject them).

scene.text: "A positive result means your life is over"
"Nothing can be done once you're positive"
"Treatment works and people live full lives"

scenarios.why: 'Your life is over' and 'nothing can be done' are false fear-talk; treatment works.
scenarios.relearn: Reject 'life is over' and 'nothing can be done'; treatment works.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two false claims about a 'cure'.

scene.text: "A herbal detox clears HIV in weeks"
"Curable STIs clear with the right antibiotics"

scenarios.why: The 'detox' and 'flush it out' lines are fake cures; only proven medicine works.
scenarios.relearn: Spot fake 'detox/flush' cures; only proven medicine controls HIV.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two myths about U=U.

scene.text: "Undetectable means it can't be passed on sexually"
"Once undetectable you can stop your medicine"

scenarios.why: 'Fully gone' and 'you can stop medicine' are wrong; the virus stays, so keep treatment.
scenarios.relearn: U=U doesn't mean gone or stop-the-pills; stay on treatment.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two unhelpful reactions to a friend's positive result.

scene.text: "Treatment works, I'll come with you to the centre"

scenarios.why: 'You did something wrong' and 'keep away' are shaming; support is the right reaction.
scenarios.relearn: Spot shaming reactions; support and dignity are the right ones.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two lines that get treatment wrong.

scene.text: "Stop the pills as soon as you feel fine"
"Ask the doctor about any side effects"

scenarios.why: 'Stop when you feel fine' and 'skipping is fine' are wrong; regular dosing keeps you well.
scenarios.relearn: Spot the 'stop when fine / skipping is fine' lies; dose regularly.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two false barriers to getting treatment.

scene.text: "It costs a fortune no one can afford"
"Everyone will find out if you go"

scenarios.why: 'Costs a fortune' and 'everyone will find out' are false; care is free and confidential.
scenarios.relearn: Spot the cost and exposure myths; care is free and confidential.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two myths about life after a diagnosis.

scene.text: "You'll be too weak to do anything"
"You can never have a partner again"

scenarios.why: 'Too weak' and 'never a partner' are myths; on treatment people live full lives.
scenarios.relearn: Spot the 'too weak / never a partner' myths; full lives are real.

scenarios.hook: Spot the two wrong ideas about STI treatment timing.

scene.text: "Early or late, it makes no difference"
"A cured STI is gone for good"
"It always comes back on its own"

scenarios.why: 'No difference' and 'comes back on its own' are wrong; early treatment cures it for good.
scenarios.relearn: Spot the 'timing doesn't matter / it returns alone' myths.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Karthik just called. His HIV test came back positive.
scenarios.setup: You meet him behind the bus stand, and he's shaking.

steps.prompt: Karthik says: "I'm finished. My whole life is finished."

options.text: "I don't know what to say. That sounds really bad."
options.then: Karthik's face crumples. "So you think so too."

options.text: "Treatment works. You've got a whole life ahead."
options.then: Karthik looks up. "Ahead? With this?"

options.text: "Calm down. Panicking won't change anything."
options.then: Karthik flinches. "Easy for you to say."

options.text: "Are you sure? Maybe the test was wrong."
options.then: Karthik clings to that for a second, then shakes his head.

steps.why: The truth that treatment works gives him something steady to hold on to.

steps.prompt: Karthik says: "Everyone will find out. People will stop talking to me."

options.text: "They might. People can be really cruel."
options.then: Karthik goes quiet, and the fear settles in deeper.

options.text: "Then don't tell anyone, ever. Not even family."
options.then: Karthik nods, but he looks even more alone.

options.text: "It's private. You decide who knows, and I'm here."
options.then: Karthik breathes out. "Okay. You're the only one so far."

options.text: "Who cares what they think? Forget them."
options.then: Karthik shakes his head. "I care. That's the whole problem."

steps.why: His status is his to share, and knowing you're there eases the fear.

steps.prompt: Karthik asks: "So what do I even do now?"

options.text: "Search online first so you know what's coming."
options.then: Karthik finds old, frightening pages and panics more.

options.text: "It's free at the centre. I'll come with you."
options.then: Karthik nods. "Tomorrow. Before I lose my nerve."

options.text: "Take some time off from everything first."
options.then: Karthik nods, and the centre feels further away each day.

options.text: "Ask my uncle. He knows a healer who cures it."
options.then: Karthik looks hopeful, and the centre drops out of his plans.

steps.why: Care at the centre is free, and going together makes it easier to walk in.

steps.prompt: Karthik asks: "Should I tell my amma?"

options.text: "No way. Parents only make things worse."
options.then: Karthik nods, and the whole load stays on him.

options.text: "If she's someone you trust, she can help. Your call."
options.then: Karthik thinks. "She'd cry. But she'd help."

options.text: "Yes. Tell her tonight, no matter what."
options.then: Karthik's breathing quickens. "Tonight? I can't."

options.text: "I'll tell her for you, so you don't have to."
options.then: Karthik panics. "No. It has to come from me."

steps.why: A trusted adult can help with care, and it's his news to share when he's ready.

scenarios.relearn: Steady a panicked friend: treatment works, it's free, and you'll go along.

scenarios.hook: You live with HIV, and your uncle has brought you a 'guaranteed' herbal cure.
scenarios.setup: He finds you alone in the kitchen.

steps.prompt: Your chacha says: "Stop those tablets. This cured a man in my village."

options.text: "Maybe. I'll think about trying yours."
options.then: Chacha beams and presses the packet into your hand.

options.text: "That man was probably never even sick."
options.then: Chacha's face darkens. "You think I'm a fool?"

options.text: "Thanks, Chacha, but I'm sticking with my treatment."
options.then: Chacha frowns. "Tablets every day, forever? This is natural."

options.text: "I'll take both. Just don't tell my doctor."
options.then: Chacha nods, pleased, and now you're keeping a secret from your doctor.

steps.why: A warm, firm 'no thanks' keeps the respect and keeps you on what works.

steps.prompt: Chacha says: "Natural is always safer than chemicals."

options.text: "Maybe you're right. Natural does sound safer."
options.then: Chacha nods, and his packet starts to look tempting.

options.text: "Natural isn't always safe. My treatment works."
options.then: Chacha grumbles, but he puts the packet down.

options.text: "You don't know anything about medicine."
options.then: Chacha bristles. "I've lived longer than you."

options.text: "I'll stop the tablets for a week and see."
options.then: Chacha grins. A week off treatment starts to feel like a plan.

steps.why: Only proven medicine controls HIV, and it's what keeps you well.

steps.prompt: Chacha says: "Don't tell your doctor about this. Doctors just want you on pills."

options.text: "Okay. It can stay between us."
options.then: Chacha nods, and now there's a secret between you and your doctor.

options.text: "Fine. I'll keep it on my shelf, just to make you happy."
options.then: The packet sits on your shelf, and Chacha asks about it every visit.

options.text: "No secrets from my doctor. I'll ask her, with Amma."
options.then: Chacha grumbles, then shrugs. "Fine. Let the doctor say it, then."

options.text: "Never bring this rubbish into our house again, Chacha."
options.then: Chacha leaves the kitchen without a word.

steps.why: Your doctor and a trusted adult can settle doubts, so you stay on treatment that works.

scenarios.relearn: Decline unproven cures kindly: stick with proven treatment.

scenarios.hook: You're undetectable on HIV treatment, and your partner Mihir has read scary posts.
scenarios.setup: He brings it up on the walk home.

steps.prompt: Mihir says: "This site says there's always some risk. Is that true?"

options.text: "Maybe. Sites like that usually know their stuff."
options.then: Mihir's worry deepens. "So we're not really safe?"

options.text: "No. Undetectable means untransmittable. It's settled."
options.then: Mihir pauses. "Settled? Then why does this site say otherwise?"

options.text: "Stop reading that stuff. It's all rubbish."
options.then: Mihir frowns. "But how do I know which part is rubbish?"

options.text: "If you're that worried, maybe we should break up."
options.then: Mihir looks stricken. "That's not what I said."

steps.why: U=U is settled science, so a clear answer meets the fear head on.

steps.prompt: Mihir asks: "How can you be sure you're still undetectable?"

options.text: "I just know. My body feels fine."
options.then: Mihir looks unconvinced. "Feeling fine isn't a test, though."

options.text: "Regular check-ups confirm it. Come to my next one."
options.then: Mihir nods slowly. "Okay. I'd like that."

options.text: "You'll have to trust me. I can't prove it."
options.then: Mihir nods, but the doubt stays on his face.

options.text: "Why? Are you calling me a liar?"
options.then: Mihir steps back. "No. I'm just scared."

steps.why: Check-ups show the treatment is working, and inviting him builds trust.

steps.prompt: Mihir says: "I still feel nervous. I don't want to rush anything."

options.text: "There's nothing to be nervous about. Just relax."
options.then: Mihir nods, but he's quiet for the rest of the walk.

options.text: "If you trusted the science, you wouldn't be nervous."
options.then: Mihir's face tightens. "So now it's my fault?"

options.text: "Then we don't rush. We go at a pace that suits us both."
options.then: Mihir's shoulders drop. "Thanks. That really helps."

options.text: "Fine. Tell me when you're over it."
options.then: Mihir looks hurt. "It's not a cold."

steps.why: U=U answers the risk, and going at both your paces respects his feelings.

scenarios.relearn: Reassure a partner with U=U: undetectable means untransmittable.

scenarios.hook: Your confirmatory HIV test is positive, and the counsellor has time for your questions.
scenarios.setup: Your mausi sits beside you in the small room.

steps.prompt: The counsellor asks: "What would you like to know first?"

options.text: "Nothing right now. Can I just go home?"
options.then: The counsellor nods gently. "Of course. Just two things first."

options.text: "What does this result mean for me, honestly?"
options.then: She nods. "It means you have HIV, and it's very treatable."

options.text: "Should I tell everyone at school straight away?"
options.then: She shakes her head gently. "That's yours to decide, later. No rush."

options.text: "Can you just tell me it's a mistake?"
options.then: She shakes her head gently. "Two tests agree. Let's go through what it means."

steps.why: Asking plainly gets you facts, which are far less frightening than guesses.

steps.prompt: The counsellor says: "Treatment is a daily tablet, and it works very well."

options.text: "Can't I wait until I actually feel sick?"
options.then: She shakes her head gently. "Starting early keeps you well."

options.text: "When can I start, and what happens next?"
options.then: She opens a calendar and walks you through the first weeks.

options.text: "Is there a quicker cure somewhere else?"
options.then: She explains there's no cure, but treatment keeps people well.

options.text: "I'll start once my exams are over."
options.then: She shakes her head gently. "Starting soon matters. We can plan it around your exams."

steps.why: Asking about next steps turns the news into a plan you can start on.

steps.prompt: The counsellor asks: "Any other questions before we finish?"

options.text: "No. I'll just look up the rest online."
options.then: She hesitates. "Lots of sites are out of date. Call me first."

options.text: "Should I stop meeting my friends, to be safe?"
options.then: She shakes her head. "Everyday contact doesn't pass it on."

options.text: "Can I still have a normal life, college and all?"
options.then: She smiles. "Yes. People on treatment live full lives."

options.text: "Is there a special diet that cures it?"
options.then: She sighs gently. "Only treatment works. Let's stick with that."

steps.why: Asking about your future gets you the true answer: treatment lets you live fully.

steps.prompt: The counsellor says: "Here's my number. Call if questions come up at home."

options.text: "I probably won't need it. I'll manage."
options.then: You leave the card behind on the chair.

options.text: "Can my friend call you with my questions?"
options.then: She smiles. "I'd rather hear them from you, or from you and Mausi."

options.text: "Thank you. Can I book my next visit now?"
options.then: She writes a date on the card, and Mausi saves it in her phone.

options.text: "I'll call once I've decided about treatment."
options.then: Her face is gentle but serious. "Let's not leave that too long."

steps.why: Booking the next visit keeps your care moving and your questions answered.

scenarios.relearn: Ask the counsellor plainly what a result means and the next steps.

scenarios.hook: In class, Rishabh jokes that anyone with HIV should 'just give up'.
scenarios.setup: A few people laugh before the teacher comes in.

steps.prompt: Rishabh says: "What? It's basically a death sentence, isn't it?"

options.text: "Ha. You're so dark, man."
options.then: Rishabh grins, and the joke keeps going round the room.

options.text: "Only if they don't look after themselves."
options.then: Rishabh shrugs. "So it's their own fault, then."

options.text: "Shut up. You're so ignorant."
options.then: Rishabh rolls his eyes. "Relax. It was a joke."

options.text: "Not anymore. Treatment works and people live full lives."
options.then: Rishabh blinks. "Full lives? I thought that was old news."

steps.why: Stating the facts calmly corrects the myth without a fight.

steps.prompt: Rishabh says: "Still, you'd keep away from someone with it, right?"

options.text: "No. Everyday contact doesn't pass it on."
options.then: Rishabh pauses. "Huh. Okay, I didn't know that."

options.text: "I mean, maybe a little. Just to be safe."
options.then: Rishabh nods, satisfied. "See? Even you agree."

options.text: "Depends who it is, I guess."
options.then: Rishabh smirks. "So you would."

options.text: "Why are you so obsessed with this?"
options.then: Rishabh shrugs, and the question goes unanswered.

steps.why: Everyday contact doesn't pass on HIV, so there's no reason to keep away.

steps.prompt: After class, Ananya says quietly: "That joke really got to me. My cousin has HIV."

options.text: "Really? Is she okay? What's it like for her?"
options.then: Ananya shifts. "She's fine. I don't really want to get into it."

options.text: "You should tell the class, so they get it."
options.then: Ananya pales. "No. It's her story, not mine."

options.text: "Wow. I'd never have guessed."
options.then: Ananya frowns. "Guessed how? There's nothing to see."

options.text: "I'm glad you told me. That joke wasn't okay."
options.then: Ananya smiles a little. "Yeah. It really wasn't."

steps.why: Listening without prying respects her and her cousin's privacy.

scenarios.relearn: Correct 'just give up' calmly: treatment works and full lives are real.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Pallavi knows you live with HIV, and she sees you take your daily tablet.
scenarios.setup: You're in her room before a sleepover movie.

steps.prompt: Pallavi asks: "You seem totally fine. Why do you still take that every day?"

options.text: "Good question. Maybe I don't need it anymore."
options.then: Pallavi shrugs. "You'd know better than me."

options.text: "Doctors just like keeping you on things."
options.then: Pallavi nods. "Yeah, my uncle says that too."

options.text: "Feeling fine is the tablet working. So I keep at it."
options.then: Pallavi thinks. "Oh. So fine means it's doing its job."

options.text: "It's complicated. You wouldn't get it."
options.then: Pallavi looks a bit hurt. "Try me."

steps.why: Feeling well is the treatment working, and daily doses keep it that way.

steps.prompt: Pallavi asks: "What happens if you miss one?"

options.text: "Nothing much. Missing a few is fine."
options.then: Pallavi nods. "Oh, cool. Easy, then."

options.text: "I double up the next day to make up for it."
options.then: Pallavi raises an eyebrow. "Is that what the doctor said?"

options.text: "My doctor told me what to do, so I follow that."
options.then: Pallavi nods. "Makes sense. They'd know."

options.text: "I'd rather not even think about that."
options.then: Pallavi drops it, and the question hangs there.

steps.why: Your doctor's plan for a missed dose is the one to follow, not a guess.

steps.prompt: Pallavi says: "My mum says HIV medicines make people really weak."

options.text: "She's probably right. I do get tired sometimes."
options.then: Pallavi looks worried. "So it's bad for you?"

options.text: "Your mum has no idea what she's talking about."
options.then: Pallavi stiffens. "Don't talk about my mum like that."

options.text: "Treatment keeps people well. I'm living proof."
options.then: Pallavi grins. "Fair. You beat me at badminton."

options.text: "Maybe I'll ask to stop them, then."
options.then: Pallavi looks unsure. "Wait. Is that a good idea?"

steps.why: Treatment keeps people well, and your own life shows it.

scenarios.relearn: Explain it simply: feeling fine is the pill working, so keep taking it.

scenarios.hook: Your test shows a treatable STI, and you need to tell Neel, who you dated recently.
scenarios.setup: You've asked him to meet at the park after school.

steps.prompt: Neel asks: "So what did you want to talk about?"

options.text: "Nothing big. Just wanted to catch up."
options.then: Neel chats about cricket until you finally blurt out the result.

options.text: "My test showed a treatable STI. You should test too."
options.then: Neel goes quiet. "Oh. Okay. Which one?"

options.text: "You gave me an STI. Thanks a lot."
options.then: Neel's face goes red. "Me? How do you know it was me?"

options.text: "Someone said you might have something."
options.then: Neel stiffens. "Who said that?" You end up telling him the real reason.

steps.why: Telling him plainly gives him what he needs to act.

steps.prompt: Neel asks: "Are you saying I gave it to you?"

options.text: "Obviously. Who else would it be?"
options.then: Neel's jaw tightens. "Wow. You've decided already."

options.text: "Maybe it was me. I'm so sorry. It's my fault."
options.then: Neel shifts, unsure what to say to that.

options.text: "I don't know, and it doesn't matter. Testing does."
options.then: Neel breathes out. "Okay. Fair."

options.text: "Let's not talk about who. Forget I said it."
options.then: Neel looks confused. "You can't just drop that on me."

steps.why: Blame helps no one. What matters is that you both get care.

steps.prompt: Neel says: "But I feel totally fine."

options.text: "Then you're probably fine. Forget it."
options.then: Neel relaxes, then hesitates. "Still. Maybe I should check."

options.text: "Fine now. It could get really bad later."
options.then: Neel goes pale. "Bad how? Now I'm scared."

options.text: "Lots of STIs have no signs. Only a test can tell."
options.then: Neel frowns. "No signs at all? Huh."

options.text: "Just get some tablets from a chemist to be safe."
options.then: Neel nods, then frowns. "Wait. Shouldn't a doctor decide that?"

steps.why: Many STIs are silent, so a test is the only way he'll know.

steps.prompt: Neel asks: "Where would I even go? I can't tell my dad."

options.text: "Then don't go. It's not worth the drama."
options.then: Neel nods, relieved, and stays untested.

options.text: "Your dad has to know. I'll tell him if you won't."
options.then: Neel goes pale. "Please don't. That's my call."

options.text: "A doctor or clinic. Maybe another adult you trust?"
options.then: Neel thinks. "My cousin's a nurse. I could ask her."

options.text: "Ask someone at your gym. They'll know a guy."
options.then: Neel looks doubtful. "A guy? For medicine?"

steps.why: A doctor can test and treat him, and a trusted adult can help him get there.

steps.prompt: When Neel finally gets tested, he texts: "Positive too, but treatable. Thanks for telling me."

options.text: "So it was you. I knew it."
options.then: Neel replies with a single "Wow" and goes quiet.

options.text: "Glad you went. Follow what the doctor said."
options.then: Neel sends a thumbs up. "Every tablet. Promise."

options.text: "Cool. Let's never talk about this again."
options.then: Neel sends a thumbs up, and neither of you mentions treatment again.

options.text: "Nice. You can stop once you feel better."
options.then: Neel hesitates. "The doctor said to finish it, though."

steps.why: Following the doctor's full course is how a treatable STI gets cleared.

scenarios.relearn: Tell a recent partner honestly so they can test and treat it too.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Senthil just tested HIV positive, and he fears the cost will ruin his family.
scenarios.setup: He's sitting on the steps outside the ration shop.

steps.prompt: Senthil says: "Appa already has loans. How will we pay for medicines for life?"

options.text: "Yeah, it's probably going to be really expensive."
options.then: Senthil's shoulders sink lower.

options.text: "HIV treatment is free at government centres."
options.then: Senthil looks up. "Free? Even the tablets?"

options.text: "Maybe skip the medicines until things are better."
options.then: Senthil looks torn. "Is that even okay?"

options.text: "Don't think about money now. It'll work out."
options.then: Senthil nods, but the worry doesn't move.

steps.why: HIV treatment is free at government centres, so cost needn't stop care.

steps.prompt: Senthil asks: "Who do I even ask about medicines without everyone knowing?"

options.text: "Ask around the market. Someone there will know."
options.then: Senthil hesitates. "Then the whole market knows my business."

options.text: "Ask the counsellor who tested you. She'll know."
options.then: Senthil nods. "She did give me a card. I'll call."

options.text: "Just ask any chemist for HIV medicine."
options.then: Senthil pictures the crowded counter and shakes his head.

options.text: "Search online and pick the cheapest clinic."
options.then: Senthil scrolls through private clinics with high fees and gets more anxious.

steps.why: The counsellor who tested him can link him to free treatment, privately.

steps.prompt: Senthil says: "Amma will be so worried when she finds out."

options.text: "Then don't tell her. Handle it all yourself."
options.then: Senthil nods, but carrying it alone looks heavy.

options.text: "Don't worry. She'll get over it eventually."
options.then: Senthil sighs. "You don't know my amma."

options.text: "Ask your uncle to break it to her for you."
options.then: Senthil hesitates. "Then it's his story to tell, not mine."

options.text: "Tell her it's free and works. I can come along."
options.then: Senthil nods slowly. "With you there, maybe I can."

steps.why: Facts about free care ease the worry, and support makes it easier to share.

scenarios.relearn: Reassure on cost: HIV treatment is free at government centres.
